newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian sugar import quota plan may be in trouble.
newsitem.headline: Russian sugar import quota plan may be in trouble.

text.p: Russia's plan to restrict refined sugar imports through quotas could be in trouble, an agriculture ministry official said on Tuesday.

Leonid Kholod, head of the ministry's price policies section, was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying a draft of the project had been presented to the government but that President Boris Yeltsin's administration had objected.
"Further movement of the document was stopped in the presidential administration," Kholod was quoted as saying, adding that "the actual question of quotas is a debatable one".
Kholod and sugar officials could not be reached for immediate comment.
The Foreign Trade Ministry last year sent an order to the government calling for white sugar imports to be set at 1.5 million tonnes a year, including 1.15 million tonnes from Ukraine.
It did not say when the quota, which must be approved by the government, would be introduced.
Interfax said ministry figures put Russia's 1996 raw sugar imports at 1.60 million tonnes, but trade and industry sources have said Russia had planned to buy 2.5 million tonnes.

Refined sugar imports over the first ten months of 1996, the last time period for which figures were available, totalled 1.30 million tonnes, mostly from Ukraine, according to Russia's Sakhar producers' union.
Ukraine's total refined sugar output fell to 3.26 million tonnes last year from 3.49 million tonnes in 1995.
